signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Downside Options Skew
signals.text: Spot trades at 157.72, holding below its SMA20 of 157.90 while a 271bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.94% vs TONA 1.23%) structurally anchors the pair. Fresh headlines confirming that Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz without US sanctions relief introduce crude supply disruption risks against a backdrop of WTI at $101.0. While VIX at 19.4 reflects normal volatility that keeps broad safe-haven flows contained, options markets show acute hedging demand via a 25d risk reversal at -2.24 and an elevated 2.1% volatility risk premium (IV 7.4% vs HV30 5.2%). JPY speculative positioning sits in the upper decile of its trailing range at pctl 94 (lev net -19,224, z +1.57), signaling vulnerability to an asymmetric squeeze if geopolitical escalation prompts official scrutiny. Downside technical focus rests on SMA50 support at 157.41, with 160.00 remaining the key psychological threshold that previously triggered official intervention warnings. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, asymmetric downside protection favored amid acute options skew. Catalyst: US ISM Manufacturing PMI and JOLTS today at 15:00 UTC. Risk: Strait of Hormuz tensions de-escalate swiftly, allowing the 271bp carry spread to reassert upward momentum.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Differential + Technical Cluster Ahead of RBA
signals.text: Spot trades at 0.7021, positioned directly above its SMA20 of 0.6996 and pressing toward the SMA50 and SMA200 resistance band at 0.7060/0.7069. Carry supports the Australian dollar, with RBA at 4.60% vs Fed at 4.00% generating a 60bp cash advantage and a 66bp OIS carry premium (AONIA 4.60% vs SOFR 3.94%). Leveraged funds maintain net long exposure at +43,927 contracts, though a WoW reduction of 3,679 contracts suggests late-trend caution as price tests moving average overhead. Short-term trend structure reflects reversal risk against the wider downtrend, further challenged by an options put skew of -0.91. A sustained daily close above the 0.7069 moving average cluster is required to confirm structural trend reversal. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; policy carry spread favors the currency into key technical resistance. Catalyst: RBA Interest Rate Decision tomorrow at 04:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds accelerate long liquidation if the RBA adopts a dovish hold tone.

signals.title: SEK — G10 Outperformance + Data Beat Momentum
signals.text: The Swedish Krona leads G10 performance over 1W, averaging +0.516% across active pairs and clearing the individual outperformance threshold against weakest peer NZD at -0.256%. Macro fundamentals underpin this outperformance, highlighted by Sweden's Economic Surprise Index at +20.0, reflecting sustained economic data beats relative to consensus forecasts. This strength emerges despite a nominal policy rate disadvantage, with the Riksbank at 1.75% sitting 225bp below the Fed's 4.00% target. In USD/SEK, spot trades at 9.813 below both its SMA20 of 9.940 and SMA50 of 9.817, confirming short-term downside momentum following a wide-range bearish expansion session. Sustained outperformance targets the 200-day moving average at 9.466 on a confirmed weekly close below 9.800. Trade bias: Bullish SEK, outperformance driven by persistent domestic macro data beats. Catalyst: Riksbank Policy Meeting on 10 Nov. Risk: Broad cross-asset risk liquidation damages European high-beta currencies.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme Speculative Short vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1198, holding below its falling SMA20 at 1.1201 and SMA50 at 1.1392 in an established technical downtrend. Institutional positioning sits at a deep historical extreme, with Leveraged Funds net short -99,557 contracts (pctl 2, z -1.78) following a WoW drop of 5,419 contracts. This institutional crowding directly opposes retail positioning, which shows an extreme 85% long bias on Retail sentiment data, setting up an acute positional divergence. Yield dynamics offer little counter-trend relief, as the Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% maintains a 135bp cash rate advantage and a 150bp OIS carry premium (SOFR 3.94% vs €STR 2.44%) favoring the dollar. Macro sentiment is further dampened by German retail sales contracting -2.0% MoM against -0.2% expected, alongside an options put skew of -0.30. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; institutional trend and 150bp carry advantage dominate retail dip-buying. Catalyst: Netherlands CPI and Spain Unemployment tomorrow morning. Risk: Leveraged funds initiate short covering, forcing a squeeze back through the SMA20 at 1.1201.
